Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:11:1.hebrew: איכא למיפרך - דאיצטריך "לא יגאל" דחרמים, דממעשר לא גמירי; דמה למעשר שכן קדש לפניו ולאחריו — שאם קרא לעשירי תשיעי, ולתשיעי עשירי, ולאחד עשר עשירי, שלשתן מקודשים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:11:1.english: It can be refuted - That "it shall not be redeemed" regarding dedications was necessary, as they could not be derived from tithe; for what is [notable] about tithe is that it is sanctified before it and after it — as if one called the tenth "ninth", and the ninth "tenth", and the eleventh "tenth", all three of them are consecrated.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:13:1.hebrew: דאיכא למיפרך - במעשר, כדפרכינן גבי חרמים: מה לבכור שכן קדושתו מרחם, תאמר במעשר שאין קדושתו מרחם? ולהכי איצטריך לא יגאל דמעשר:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:13:1.english: As it can be refuted - With regard to [animal] tithe, just as we refuted regarding dedications: What [is notable] about a firstborn? That its sanctity is from the womb. Shall you say [the same] of [animal] tithe, whose sanctity is not from the womb? And for this [reason], “It shall not be redeemed” regarding [animal] tithe was necessary.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:16:1.hebrew: והעברת קרא יתירא הוא - ומופנה לגזירה שוה, ללמד העברה העברה על מעשר שלא יגאל, ואין משיבין עליה; הילכך, לא יגאל דמעשר מופנה הוא. ומאי טעמא האי קרא יתירא? דמצי למכתב: כל פטר רחם לה', כדכתיב קרא אחרינא (שמות יג): כל פטר רחם לה'. והעברת למה לי? ש"מ, קרא יתירא הוא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:16:1.english: “And you shall cause to pass” is a superfluous verse - And [it is therefore] free for the verbal analogy, to teach [from the common term of] “passing” [and] “passing” concerning [animal] tithe that it may not be redeemed, and one cannot refute it; consequently, “it shall not be redeemed” of [animal] tithe is free. And what is the reason that this verse is superfluous? For it could have written: “All that opens the womb [shall be] to the Lord,” just as another verse states (Exodus 13): “all that opens the womb... to the Lord.” Why do I need “And you shall cause to pass”? Conclude from it [that] it is a superfluous verse.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:17:1.hebrew: בכור נמי נילף גאולה גאולה מחרמים - דלא ימכר, דאע"ג דלא כתב בבכור גאולה, כתב ביה פדייה (שם), והיא היא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:17:1.english: With regard to a firstborn as well, let us derive "redemption," "redemption" from dedications - [To teach] that it may not be sold. For even though [the term] "redemption" [ge'ulah] is not written regarding a firstborn, "redemption" [pediyyah] is written regarding it (there), and it is one and the same.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:17:2.hebrew: גאולה דמעשר מפני - כדאמרן, הלכך דיינינן ליה גזירה שוה מחרמים. אבל פדייה דבכור לא מפני, דאיצטריך לגופיה, ולאגמורי נמי אמעשר בהעברה העברה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:17:2.english: The redemption of [animal] tithe is free - As we have said; therefore, we derive for it a verbal analogy from dedicated items. However, the redemption of a firstborn is not free, as it was needed for itself, and also to teach regarding [animal] tithe via [the verbal analogy of] "passing" [and] "passing".

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:18:1.hebrew: ומאי חזית - דפדייה דבכור לגופיה ולאגמורי אמעשר, ולא יגאל דמעשר לאפנויי ולמיגמר גזירה שוה מחרמים? אימא: לא יגאל דמעשר לגופיה — דלא יפדה — ולאגמורי אבכור בהעברה העברה, ודבכור לאפנויי ולמיגמר גזירה שוה מחרמים, דאסור במכירה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:18:1.english: And what did you see - That [the law of] redemption of a firstborn is [necessary] for itself and to teach about [animal] tithe, and “it shall not be redeemed” of [animal] tithe is free to derive a verbal analogy [*gezeirah shavah*] from devoted items? Say [instead]: “It shall not be redeemed” of [animal] tithe is [necessary] for itself — that it may not be redeemed — and to teach about a firstborn through [the verbal analogy of] *ha’avarah* *ha’avarah*; and that of a firstborn is free to derive a verbal analogy [*gezeirah shavah*] from devoted items, [namely] that it is forbidden to be sold.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:1:1.hebrew: ושאינו נישום מחיים - כגון העור והגידין, שחשיבות שום דמי הבהמה אינו בשביל העור; הלכך, בהבלעה שרי, אפי' דגדול. וביתמי, משום השבת אבידה, אוקמוה אדאורייתא — דלאחר שחיטה מוכרו כדרכו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:1:1.english: And [an item] that is not appraised while alive - such as the hide and the sinews, as the principal appraisal of the animal’s value is not on account of the hide. Therefore, by inclusion [in the hide], it is permitted, even [for] an adult. And with orphans, on account of restoring a loss, they established [the law] according to Torah law — that after slaughter, one may sell it in its [ordinary] manner.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:22:1.hebrew: ונילף בכור העברה ממעשר - שיהא אסור במכירה, דהא מעשר כבר קים לן דגמרנא ליה גאולה מחרמים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:22:1.english: And let [us] derive [regarding] a firstborn [by the verbal analogy of] "passing" from [animal] tithe - That it should be prohibited from sale, as [regarding animal] tithe, it is already established for us that we derived it [by the verbal analogy of] "redemption" from dedications.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:23:1.hebrew: מסתברא מעשר - הוה ליה לרבויי בדין חרמים, דגאולה כתב ביה כמו בחרמים, ולמעוטי בכור, דפדייה כתב ביה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:23:1.english: It is logical [to include] tithe - It ought to include [tithe] under the law of dedications, for [the term of] redemption [ge’ulah] is written regarding it just as regarding dedications, and to exclude a firstborn, for [the term of] redemption [pediyyah] is written regarding it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:24:1.hebrew: לא יגאל דחרמים לא צריך - ולא משום דגמר מבכור, אלא מסברא נפקא לן דאינו בפדייה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:24:1.english: “It may not be redeemed” regarding dedications is unnecessary - And [this is] not because it is derived from a firstborn; rather, we derive from logical reasoning that it is not subject to redemption:

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:24:2.hebrew: הקדש נינהו - ואינו בפדייה, ולא דמי לקדשי מזבח:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:24:2.english: They are consecrated [property] - And it is not subject to redemption, and it is not similar to offerings for the altar.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:24:3.english: They are non-sacred - And the priest may sell them to whomever he wishes.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:25:1.english: Every dedicated item is holy - It is forbidden to be sold.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:25:2.english: Shall be yours - In the possession of the priest, they are like the rest of his property.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:2:1.hebrew: סבר לה להא דרבא - דמעשר לאחר שחיטה, דאורייתא שרי למכור:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:2:1.english: Holds in accordance with that [opinion] of Rava - That [with regard to] an animal tithe after slaughter, by Torah law it is permitted to sell [it].

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:3:1.hebrew: רק בכל אות נפשך - מוקמינן בספרי דבפסולי המוקדשין מישתעי, וכתיב: "תזבח ואכלת":
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:3:1.english: Notwithstanding, after all the desire of your soul - We establish in the Sifrei that [the verse] is speaking of disqualified consecrated animals, and it is written: “You may slaughter and eat [flesh].”

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:3:2.hebrew: איזהו דבר שאין בו ברכה מחיים - שאין נהנין מהם מחיים, דהא שאר קדשים, אם נפל בהן מום — פודן, ויכול למוכרן מחיים לכל מי שירצה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:3:2.english: Which is the item that has no blessing while alive - That one may not derive benefit from them while alive; for behold, [regarding] other consecrated animals, if a blemish befell them, one redeems them and can sell them while alive to whomever he wishes.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:3:3.hebrew: אלא זה מעשר בהמה - דכתיב ביה לא יגאל, דאינו נמכר מחיים, וכתב דלאחר זביחה איכא ברכה. וההוא ברכה מכירה היא — דדומיא דברכה שאסר לך מחיים התיר לך לאחר שחיטה, ומה ברכה היתה ראויה בו מחיים? מכירה. אלמא לאחר שחיטה נמכר מדאורייתא, והא דתני אינו נמכר שחוט — דרבנן הוא; הילכך, ביתמי מוקמינן אדאורייתא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:3:3.english: Rather, this is the animal tithe - For it is written concerning it: “It shall not be redeemed,” meaning that it may not be sold alive, and [the verse] writes that after slaughter there is a blessing. And that blessing is sale, for similar to the blessing that [the Torah] forbade to you while [the animal was] alive, it permitted to you after slaughter; and what blessing would have been appropriate for it while alive? Sale. Evidently, after slaughter it may be sold by Torah law, and that which was taught, that it may not be sold slaughtered, is rabbinic; therefore, in the case of orphans, we establish [the halakha] according to Torah law.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:4:1.english: What is [the halakha with regard to] including [it] - The value of the meat of an animal tithe of a large [animal] together with the value of the bones.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:5:1.hebrew: דקה - אין העצמות ראויים לכלום, ואין מבליעין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:5:1.english: A small [animal] - The bones are not fit for anything, and one does not include [the value in them].

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:5:2.hebrew: גסה - ראויין העצמות לקתתא דנגרי וחציני, ומבליעין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:5:2.english: [A] large [animal] - The bones are suitable for the handles of adzes and axes, and [therefore] one may include [the value of the meat in them]:

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:6:1.hebrew: באתריה דמר - עושין כלים מעצמות, ובאתריה דמר אין עושין כלים מעצמות, ואין מבליעין:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:6:1.english: In the locale of [one] Master - they fashion utensils from bones, and in the locale of the [other] Master they do not fashion utensils from bones, and [therefore] they do not include [the value of the meat in them].

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:7:1.hebrew: מנא ה"מ - דמעשר אינו נמכר, דמאי משמע מכירה מלא יגאל:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:7:1.english: From where are these matters [derived] - That [animal] tithe is not sold — for how does "it shall not be redeemed" imply sale?

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:8:1.english: With regard to dedications - It is written (Leviticus 27:28): “It shall not be sold and it shall not be redeemed; every dedicated item is most holy…”

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:9:1.english: Free - That it is necessary that these words, “it shall not be redeemed,” be free for this exposition.

Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:9:2.hebrew: שכן חלין על הכל - שאם החרים את הקדשים, חל חרם עליהן, ונותן לכהן כפי טובת הנאה שיש לו בהן, כדאמר בערכין בפ' המקדיש שדהו (ערכין דף כח:). תאמר במעשר, שאינו חל אלא על החולין? ועוד: חרם חל על כל העדר, ומעשר אינו אלא עשירי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 32a:9:2.english: For they apply to all - For if one dedicated consecrated items as a cherem, the cherem takes effect upon them, and he gives [the value] to the priest according to the benefit of discretion that he has in them, as [the Gemara] says in Arakhin in the chapter [entitled] Hamakdish Sedeihu (Arakhin 28b). Can you say [the same] of [animal] tithe, which takes effect only upon non-sacred [animals]? And furthermore, a cherem takes effect upon the entire herd, whereas [animal] tithe is only the tenth [animal].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:10:1.hebrew: דלא יאמר לא יגאל בחרמים וגמר ממעשר מה מעשר קדוש ואינו נגאל - וא"ת: דילמא הוה ילפינן מהקדש, דתפדה? וי"ל: דלחומרא ילפינן. א"נ: משום דבחרמים כתיב "לא ימכר", ומוקמינן בהו "לא יגאל":
Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:10:1.english: "Let [the verse] not state 'it shall not be redeemed' with regard to dedications, and let it derive [it] from tithe: Just as tithe is sacred and cannot be redeemed" - And if you say: Perhaps we would have derived [it] from [ordinary] consecrated property, that it may be redeemed? And one can say: We derive [the law in favor of] stringency. Alternatively, [it is] because regarding dedications it is written: "It shall not be sold," and [so] we establish in their case [that] "it shall not be redeemed."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:23:1.hebrew: הוא ולא בכור - רבא נמי דמשני בסמוך: "שלא ימכר" בחרמים לא צריך — אית ליה נמי "הוא ולא בכור", כדמוכח בפ"ק דתמורה (דף ה:) גבי "אי עביד לא מהני"; דאי לאו "הוא", הוה ילפינן בכור "העברה" "העברה" ממעשר. ואביי נמי דמוקי בפ"ק דתמורה: "הוא" — בהוייתו יהא, מ"מ הוה דריש "הוא ולא בכור", מדסמך ליה "הוא" ל"קדש קדשים", דמשמע: הוא בקדושתו יהא:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:23:1.english: “It, but not a firstborn” - Rava too, who explains nearby that “[the prohibition] that it may not be sold” regarding dedications is not needed, also holds [the derivation of] “it, but not a firstborn,” as is proven in the first chapter of Temurah (5b) regarding [the principle of] “if one did [it], it does not take effect”; for were it not for “it,” we would have derived [that] a firstborn [may not be sold via the verbal analogy of] ha’avarah, ha’avarah from [animal] tithe. And Abaye too, who establishes in the first chapter of Temurah [that the word] “it” [means] “it shall remain in its state,” nevertheless would expound “it, but not a firstborn,” since [the verse] juxtaposed “it” to “most holy,” which implies: it [alone] shall remain in its sanctity.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:24:1.hebrew: רבא אמר לא יגאל דחרמים לא צריך - כך כתוב בספרים. ורש"י גרס "לא ימכר", משום דדייק: דאיתנהו היכא? אי בי בעלים — הקדש נינהו! ואי ב"לא יגאל" קאמר — והא קדשי בדק הבית נגאלין! ור"ת מפ': "דהקדש נינהו" קאמר — היינו אפי' נפדו, ד"קדש קדשים" משמע ליה קדושת הגוף עד בואו ליד כהן. ומיהו קשיא לר', דבפ"ק דתמורה (דף ה:) משמע דמוכחינן דאין מועיל פדיון מ"הוא" — "בהוייתו יהא", לאביי ד"אי עביד מהני"; ולרבא דאמר "לא מהני", נפיק מ"לא יגאל" גופיה. וא"כ היכי הוה דייק הכא ד"לא יגאל" לא צריך משום דאי בי בעלים הקדש נינהו, אפילו נפדו — הוא גופה מ"לא יגאל" נפקא ליה לרבא?! ועוד קשיא אחרת שהקשה רש"י: הא דקאמר "אם אינו ענין לחרמים תנהו ענין למעשר", מאי צריך מעשר ל"לא יגאל" דחרמים? הא בגופה כתב! ואי משום "לא ימכר" בקנייה, הכי ה"ל למימר: "ואם אינו ענין לגאולה דבגופה כתב, תנהו ענין למכירה"; א"נ יאמר: "לא יגאל" דחרמים למה לי? ש"מ לאפנויי:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:24:1.english: Rava says: “It shall not be redeemed” regarding dedications is unnecessary - So it is written in the books [i.e., manuscripts]. But Rashi had the reading: “It shall not be sold,” because [Rava] deduced: “Where are they? If they are in the owner’s possession, they are consecrated [and consecrated items cannot be sold]!” And if [Rava] was speaking of “it shall not be redeemed,” behold, items consecrated to the Temple treasury can be redeemed! And Rabbeinu Tam explains: When [Rava] says “they are consecrated,” this means even if they were redeemed [the redemption does not take effect], for “it is most holy” implies to him bodily sanctity until it comes into the priest’s possession. However, this is difficult to the Rabbi, for in the first chapter of Temurah (5b) it implies that we deduce that redemption is ineffective from “it [is most holy]” — [meaning] “it shall remain in its state,” according to Abaye, who holds that if one performs [a prohibited act], it is effective; but according to Rava, who says that [a prohibited act] is not effective, it is derived from “it shall not be redeemed” itself. And if so, how could Rava deduce here that “it shall not be redeemed” is unnecessary because if they are in the owner’s possession they are consecrated, even if they were redeemed — when that itself is derived for Rava from “it shall not be redeemed”?! And furthermore, there is another difficulty that Rashi raised: As for that which [the Gemara] says, “If it is not relevant to dedications, apply it to [animal] tithe” — why does [animal] tithe need the “it shall not be redeemed” of dedications? Behold, it is written in its own context! And if [it is derived] because of “it shall not be sold” through acquisition, this is what it should have said: “And if it is not relevant to redemption, which is written in its own context, apply it to sale.” Alternatively, let it say: Why do I need “it shall not be redeemed” regarding dedications? Learn from it that it is to make [the term] free [for the verbal analogy].

Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:2:1.hebrew: ואף רב שמואל בר רב יצחק סבר לה להא דרבא - פי': מקרא אחרינא, ולא מטעמיה:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 32a:2:1.english: “And even Rav Shmuel bar Rav Yitzḥak holds in accordance with that [opinion] of Rava” - Explanation: [He derives it] from another verse, and not from his [Rava’s] reason.
